items.title: Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT's new biology skills wow scientists
items.excerpt: Anthropic and OpenAI's general language models can now design proteins and predict their sequences and structures, capabilities previously seen only in specialized tools; OpenAI reports GPT-6 designs that bound targets in lab tests.

history_match.title: AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more

items.title: Scientists discover protein knot once thought impossible – thanks to AI
items.excerpt: Polish researchers, following up AI structure-prediction 'hallucinations', describe in PNAS a protein family with an eight-crossing knot, the most complex protein knot identified to date. (Off-list: no on-list outlet carried it.)

items.title: Supervised deep learning for efficient cryo-EM image alignment in drug discovery with cryoPARES
items.excerpt: cryoPARES uses supervised deep learning to align cryo-EM particle images, removing computational bottlenecks and manual intervention for high-throughput structure determination.

items.title: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
items.excerpt: Researchers build DNA-strand-displacement 'neurons' with heterogeneous thresholds and wire them into molecular neural networks that adapt their computation to the chemical environment (date via Crossref created).

history_match.title: Quantum neural networks with high-dimensional quantum neurons

items.title: AI helps researchers track beluga whales using aerial drone images
items.excerpt: Florida Atlantic University and Fisheries and Oceans Canada used semi-supervised deep learning (SEMI-DETR) to detect and track belugas and calves across drone image sequences with 5-10x less hand labeling (Frontiers in Marine Science).

items.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
items.excerpt: Teams of Gemini 4 agents improved known quantum algorithms, cutting a fusion-energy circuit cost 11.8x, a photosensitive-molecule simulation 8x and a Cytochrome P450 simulation 2.5x, each proven correct in Lean (arXiv 2611.09822).

history_match.title: Google Researchers Use AI And Mathematical Proofs to Cut Quantum Computing Requirements

items.title: Researchers Fit Quantum Circuits Into a 30 Billion-Parameter AI Model
items.excerpt: Researchers replaced eight layers of the Qwen3 language model with a module that can run on a quantum processor, testing hybrid quantum circuits inside a 30B-parameter model.

items.title: Machine-learning models can detect elevated psychopathy and sadism from reactions to funny pictures
items.excerpt: Algorithms trained on people's ratings of memes and cartoons flagged elevated psychopathy, sadism and narcissism, while Machiavellianism left no detectable trace.

items.title: Chatbots can quash emerging conspiracy theories
items.excerpt: Cornell researchers found AI chatbot conversations talked about 15% of people out of conspiracy beliefs in the immediate aftermath of a crisis, when little information is known. (Off-list: no on-list outlet had it yet.)

items.title: Physics-guided AI reconstructs fluid flow from sparse, noisy data
items.excerpt: UC Irvine's PMPG-NN couples a neural network with the principle of minimum pressure gradient to reconstruct physically consistent flow fields from sparse, noisy measurements without pressure data (Physics of Fluids).

items.title: Predicting the unknown: A robust approach lets AI extrapolate to undiscovered materials
items.excerpt: University of Tokyo researchers decouple structure learning (pretrained graph neural networks) from property regression, cutting extrapolation error 68% versus CGCNN on newer Materials Project entries (PRX Intelligence).

items.title: A legendary philosopher isn't buying Anthropic's consciousness argument
items.excerpt: Anthropic warned investors its AI might be conscious; a leading philosopher of mind pushes back on the argument and what acting on it would mean.

items.title: AI is 'the end of mathematics as we know it' — where does the field go next?
items.excerpt: After AI-assisted proofs of Riemann-class problems, mathematicians brace for a future in which much of their profession could be delegated to machines.
